items.title: PM Modi free recharge claim fake: PIB Fact Check
items.snippet_en: Prabhat Khabar reported that PIB Fact Check clarified that neither the Prime Minister nor the central government is running any such scheme, and there has been no official announcement or confirmation from any telecom company.

items.title: PM Narendra Modi Offering Free Recharge of Rs 239? No, This Claim is Fake
items.snippet_en: The Quint reported that a fake post was being shared, falsely claiming PM Modi was offering free Rs 239 recharge to voters ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha Elections. PIB had debunked similar claims, stating that the Indian government has not announced any free recharge scheme.

items.title: This WhatsApp message about government's free recharge scheme is fake
items.snippet_en: IndiaTimes reported that a fake message offering free recharge by PM Narendra Modi circulating on WhatsApp was debunked by PIB Fact Check. The scam claims to provide 3 months of free mobile recharge as part of a government scheme, prompting users to click on a fraudulent link.

items.title: Govt debunks fake video claiming PM Modi announced free three-month recharge
items.snippet_en: NewsOnAir reported that the government debunked a video circulating on social media claiming that Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a free three-month recharge for all citizens. The PIB Fact Check Unit stated that the claim is fake and the viral video is AI-generated.

items.title: PM Modi Offering Free Recharge On Returning To Power? A Fact Check
items.snippet_en: NDTV reported that multiple posts claiming PM Modi and BJP are offering free mobile recharge for three months to every Indian as a reward for winning the 2024 elections are fake. Neither PM Narendra Modi nor the BJP has announced any such scheme.

outputs.notes_en: Multiple sources, including PIB Fact Check, confirm that the claim of Prime Minister Modi providing free mobile recharge is false. These claims are often part of scams designed to collect user data or lead to financial fraud.
